title: Wire Under the Big Top
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk, Pei Lie（Ringmaster Pei Lie in his fifties, gray buzz cut, deep-red tailcoat and black vest, a gilt whistle pinned to his chest, hands covered in calluses and old scars） lifts the flap and enters the circus big top（Inside the red-and-white striped circus big top, rings and safety net hang from the dome, a performance circle drawn on the sand floor）; the aerial rings（A pair of aerial rings suspended from the big-top dome, chrome steel rings intact, hemp rope taut and gleaming, magnesium light making the rings snow-bright） hang taut and gleaming under dome magnesium light.

A row of five magnesium floodlights（A row of five magnesium floodlights hung from the big-top steel beams, shades polished clear） hangs from the big-top steel beams; Pei Lie polishes each lamp shade one by one.

Two opening gongs（Two opening gongs hanging at the circus big-top entrance, faces chased with the character for 'star', trembling lightly when the wind rises） hang at the tent entrance; Pei Lie reaches up and lets the gong faces tremble softly.
Pei Lie walks the shadow of the aerial rings, checking hemp-rope tension and safety clasps.
Pei Lie gazes out the tent door at the sky over the practice yard.
The intact aerial rings hang quietly from the circus big-top dome.
Pei Lie sits at the sand's edge and dozes in the magnesium light.
Night wind pours through the tent door; Pei Lie pulls his tailcoat collar tight.
Pei Lie opens the show rehearsal book（A hardcover show rehearsal book, circus emblem on the cover, pages marked in red pen with beats and blocking） and marks the evening's beats in red pen.
Pei Lie draws a blocking arc on the show rehearsal book.
Pei Lie closes the show rehearsal book and puts it in the director's desk drawer.
Magnesium light from the aerial rings sweeps across Pei Lie's profile.
Pei Lie wipes fingerprints from the gilt whistle with a soft cloth.

At dawn in the outdoor practice yard（The packed-earth practice yard outside the tent, old mats laid out, a portable high-low bar standing to one side）, Pei Lie welcomes young Annuan（Young Annuan: a fifteen-year-old lean aerial apprentice, coral-red hair ribbon, cream practice leotard, cyan ankle guard on her left ankle, bright stubborn eyes） arriving on the vermilion Spark Star（A vermilion circus carriage, doors spray-painted with gold letters 'Spark Star', triangular pennant on the roof, prop crates inside）.
Annuan hops down from Spark Star and reties her coral-red hair ribbon.

Pei Lie points at the three balance balls（Three red-and-blue balance balls, arranged by size at the edge of the practice-yard mats） by the mats and teaches Annuan to read center of gravity and landing points.
Annuan crouches on the old mat, curiously tracing the wear marks on the high-low bar.
Pei Lie points at the circus big-top dome and explains the aerial rings opening to Annuan.
Annuan looks back at Spark Star parked nearby, eyes full of longing.
The two stand shoulder to shoulder by the portable high-low bar, listening to the canvas snap in the wind.

In the props alley（A narrow alley behind the tent leading to the prop store, fake flowers and fire hoops stacked on both sides, pine-resin smell in the air）, indigo-ribboned Anchuan（Young Anchuan: face extremely similar to Annuan's, but indigo hair ribbon, silver bell ankle guard on right ankle, more playful expression） glances back from behind the fake flowers.
Anchuan fiddles with a fire hoop in the alley, bell ankle guard chiming softly.
Anchuan snaps a photo of an old poster on the wall with his phone and laughs playfully.
Anchuan carries a white-face paint box through the shadows of the props alley.
Pine-resin smell fills the air; Anchuan stops to listen to the creak of rings overhead.
On the outdoor practice yard, Annuan and Anchuan stand side by side, one coral-red ribbon, one indigo ribbon.
Annuan hands a balance ball to Anchuan; they smile at each other.
Anchuan straightens Annuan's hair ribbon; the two walk slowly along the mat edge.
Annuan and Anchuan part at the west end of the practice yard, each heading the opposite way.
Dust rises; their retreating backs, one red ribbon, one blue, pull farther apart.
Months later at night, Pei Lie keeps watch alone in the circus big top; the aerial rings hang quietly.

Pei Lie opens the show rehearsal book（The same show rehearsal book stained when paint was knocked over, cover sticky, writing blurred into color patches） and finds the cover stained by spilled paint, writing blurred into color patches.
Pei Lie wipes magnesium powder from the aerial rings hemp rope.
Pei Lie stands by the tent door, gazing at the dark practice yard.
The outline of the aerial rings slowly emerges in the magnesium light.
Pei Lie slips the stained show rehearsal book into a leather sleeve and sighs.
Seasons turn; day after day Pei Lie lifts the flap and enters the circus big top.
On another snow night, Pei Lie wraps his tailcoat tight under the aerial rings.
Spring tour opens; Pei Lie calibrates the safety net at center sand.
Midsummer noon, Pei Lie wipes the sun-scorched iron stakes outside the tent.
Autumn rains linger; the aerial rings hemp rope turns stiff in the damp.
On another New Year's Eve, Pei Lie keeps the circus big top alone until dawn.
On the extra-show eve, Pei Lie checks safety clasps two hours early.
On a full-moon night, Pei Lie test-lights every magnesium floodlight.
Three showless nights in a row, Pei Lie revises the blocking chart again and again.
One windy night, Pei Lie has to tie down the tent ropes extra tight.
Rope creaks; Pei Lie looks up quickly to check the aerial rings.
At three in the morning, Pei Lie sips cold tea from a thermos.
He sorts balance ball numbers at the director's desk.
Opening gongs tremble softly in the wind; Pei Lie lifts his head to listen.
As the horizon pales, Pei Lie notes the last beat group of the night.
Before lowering the canvas, he takes one last look at the intact hemp rope on the aerial rings.
At daybreak, Pei Lie patrols the outdoor practice yard; vermilion Spark Star is parked by the high-low bar.
Pei Lie crouches to inspect Spark Star's shaft and pennant.
Pei Lie walks to the mat edge; the same three balance balls still stand in neat order.

An unfamiliar ochre props truck（An unfamiliar ochre props pickup with mats in the bed, no Spark Star lettering on the body, definitely not Spark Star） drives along the camp road, mats in the bed, not Spark Star.
Pei Lie stands on the packed-earth yard, recording last night's peak wind speed.
Pei Lie realigns the edges of the old mats.
Morning mist recedes in the distance, revealing deeper riverbank shadows.
A storm bursts; the circus big top billows in gale wind; the aerial rings swing violently.
Magnesium light flickers wildly; Pei Lie rushes to the emergency winch.
A dull crack—the aerial rings（The same aerial rings with frayed worn hemp rope, rings tilted, tension slack so they sway） hemp rope frays and wears, rings tilting and swaying.
On the camp road, vermilion Spark Star shakes violently in the jolts.
A side roll breaks Spark Star（The vermilion carriage with broken shaft overturned, pennant snapped, an un-tourable wreck）'s shaft and overturns it; the pennant snaps.
Inside the big top, Pei Lie lunges for the aerial rings safety clasp and steadies the swaying rings.
The day after the storm, Pei Lie stands in the circus big top, staring at the worn aerial rings.
Pei Lie runs a finger over the frayed hemp rope, face downcast.
Pei Lie notes the date of Spark Star's broken shaft on a slip beside the show rehearsal book.
An old photo of Spark Star hangs on the tent wall; Pei Lie gazes at it for a long time.
Pei Lie takes one of the five magnesium floodlights from the dome and sits alone in its dim glow.
The damaged aerial rings still hang tilted from the circus big-top dome.
Weeks later, Pei Lie brings new hemp rope and a splicing knife to repair the aerial rings.

Pei Lie takes a pair of practice rings（A waist-high pair of practice rings shaped much like the aerial rings but with shorter rope and plastic rings） from a wooden crate—they look like the aerial rings but with shorter rope.
Pei Lie carefully replaces the rope, splices knots, and retensions the line.

The last knot tightens; the aerial rings（The aerial rings with new hemp rope restored to tautness, fresh rope knots on the rings, distinct from the original intact state） reach the rope-replaced state.
The repaired aerial rings hang steady again; Pei Lie watches them with relief.

A silver-gray Luminous Stream parade cart（A brand-new silver-gray parade electric cart spray-painted 'Luminous Stream', no carriage shaft, utterly unlike Spark Star） rolls onto the outdoor practice yard, nothing like the broken-shaft Spark Star.

Supervisor Chao（Supervisor Chao the touring inspector in his fifties, gray buzz cut and deep-red tailcoat like Pei Lie's build, but silver supervisor embroidery on the cuffs） walks onto the practice yard and talks beside Pei Lie; the two builds are much alike.
Supervisor Chao points at the Luminous Stream parade cart and explains the new touring schedule to Pei Lie.
The Luminous Stream parade cart drives away; Pei Lie stays alone on the practice yard watching it go.
Wind flaps the schedule sheet Supervisor Chao left behind.

Outside camp arrives Tangtang the acrobatics school girl（Tangtang the acrobatics school girl, fifteen or sixteen, coral-red hair ribbon; at a glance somewhat like young Annuan, but no cyan ankle guard on the left and shy timid eyes） with a coral-red ribbon; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Annuan.
Tangtang the acrobatics school girl tries a stretch; Pei Lie shakes his head—she is not Annuan after all.
Tangtang the acrobatics school girl carries her practice shoes away from the outdoor practice yard, back fading down the camp road.

Years later at dusk, Pei Lie（The same Pei Lie injured: right leg in a splint, leaning on a black lacquer cane as he walks slowly, still wearing that faded deep-red tailcoat） with a splinted right leg stands at the circus big-top entrance leaning on a black lacquer cane.
Cane in hand, Pei Lie looks up at the red-and-white striped dome, gaze far away.
The two opening gongs at the entrance tremble softly in the wind; Pei Lie pauses on his cane to listen.
Cane in hand, Pei Lie presses his palm beside the cool founding plaque on the doorpost, as if saying goodbye.
He slowly sits on a wooden crate on the practice yard, splinted leg stretched straight.

By day, adult Annuan（Adult Annuan: a supple aerial lead in her twenties, still with coral-red hair ribbon and cyan left ankle guard, expression steady） comes back along the camp road, hurrying toward the circus big top.
Annuan reunites with cane-leaning Pei Lie outside the tent; they embrace.
Beside the narrow couch in the dressing room, Annuan holds Pei Lie's calloused yet cold hand.

Pei Lie（Pei Lie has closed his eyes and passed away, lying quietly on the narrow couch in the dressing room behind the tent, face peaceful, breath gone）'s breath fades; at last he closes his eyes and passes away.
Annuan gently sets Pei Lie's gilt whistle back on the pillow.
Pei Lie's deep-red tailcoat still hangs behind the tent door; Annuan reaches out and touches it lightly.

By the doorpost, adult Annuan stands before a newly nailed founding plaque（A founding plaque nailed to the tent doorpost, carved with Pei Lie's name and the year the troupe was founded, edges green with patina）.
Annuan's fingertips trace Pei Lie's name carved on the founding plaque.
Wind rises; opening gongs tremble faintly in the distance; Annuan lifts her head.

Adult Anchuan（Adult Anchuan: face extremely similar to adult Annuan's, still indigo ribbon and bell ankle guard, half the face painted white） arrives from a neighboring troupe and embraces Annuan tightly under the circus big-top door.
Annuan and Anchuan stand side by side by the doorpost, one steady, one playful.
The two look at each other in silence, studying faces alike yet different.
Anchuan lifts a white-face brush but sets it down again, simply standing with Annuan.
The camera returns to years ago—the youth on the old mat tracing wear marks on the high-low bar appears again.
The opening moment returns—in the big top, a chrome-steel ring pair is tensioned for the first time.
Flash back to the props alley of that year—a figure with indigo ribbon and bell ankle guard flashes past.
Before the eyes rises again that row of five old magnesium floodlights on the dome.
Return to the packed-earth practice yard at first meeting, old mats spread as they once were.
Annuan opens the paint-stained show rehearsal book again and walks into the circus big top.
By the mats, the same three balance balls still stand in neat order.
Annuan takes up the watch over the aerial rings; magnesium light brightens the ring faces again.
Outside the tent, red-and-white stripes snap in the morning wind.
